title: Chickpea Shakshuka with Goat Cheese
changes_from_base: Chickpeas and roasted red peppers bulk out a quick smoked-paprika and crushed-tomato sauce; eight eggs are cooked until the whites are fully set, then finished with goat cheese and olive oil.
summary: A filling shakshuka of tender chickpeas in a spiced tomato sauce, crowned with creamy goat cheese.
equipment: 30 cm non-stick frying pan with a lid

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus extra to drizzle
jarred roasted red peppers, rinsed, patted dry and roughly chopped
fine sea salt or table salt
x 400 g tin chickpeas, rinsed (240 g drained)

steps.title: Heat Oil
steps.text: Heat 30 ml extra-virgin olive oil in a 30 cm non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.

steps.title: Sauté Base
steps.text: Add 1 finely chopped medium onion (about 150 g), 140 g rinsed and patted-dry jarred roasted red peppers (roughly chopped), 1 tsp fine salt and ½ tsp ground black pepper, cooking about 4 minutes until the onion softens.

steps.title: Add Spices
steps.text: Add 1 rinsed 400 g tin of chickpeas (240 g drained), 1½ tsp smoked paprika and 1 tsp ground cumin and cook 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.title: Tomatoes
steps.text: Stir in 800 g tinned crushed tomatoes, bring to a simmer, cover, lower the heat to medium-low and cook 5 minutes.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Off the heat, make 8 shallow 4 cm hollows (7 around the edge, 1 in the middle), crack a large egg into each and spoon sauce over the edges of the whites.

steps.title: Cook Eggs
steps.text: Return to medium-high heat, bring to a simmer, lower to medium-low, cover and cook about 8 minutes, turning the pan occasionally, until the egg whites are fully set.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Scatter 57 g crumbled soft goat cheese over the eggs, drizzle with a little extra oil and serve straight away.

tips: Pat the roasted peppers dry before chopping so the sauce doesn't become too watery
Turn the pan occasionally as it cooks to ensure even cooking of the eggs
safety: The yolks stay soft once the whites set; for pregnant, very young, elderly or immunocompromised eaters, cook on until the yolks are firm (71 °C)
storage: Serve straight away. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
